humanTitle: People cannot reach tickets they have already paid for
whoItAffects: Mostly Android users, across three app versions, blocked at the sign-in screen.

build.proposition: A ticket that still works when the app does not.
specifics: Issue a wallet pass at purchase, before any sign-in is required
Keep the barcode on the device rather than behind a live session
Start with the failed-login path reviewers describe at the gate
build.limitation: A wallet pass is easier to forward, which is the thing app-only ticketing exists to prevent.

start.proposition: Not a company so much as a term venues could insist on.
specifics: Venues contract for an offline fallback at the gate
Pitched as queue time saved rather than as software
start.limitation: The app is usually chosen by whoever sells the event, not by the venue that would want this.

study.proposition: Does app-only ticketing move the risk of failure onto the ticket holder?
specifics: Compare entry failures at app-only events against printable ones
Ask people turned away at a gate what they were told
study.limitation: Entry failures are not logged anywhere a researcher can reach, so this rests on recall.

write.proposition: You bought the ticket. The app decides whether you get in.
specifics: Open at a gate with someone whose login is failing
Use the reviews where reinstalling changed nothing
write.limitation: Ticketing complaints are a familiar genre; the sharper story here is the sign-in, not the fees.
